messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Helpers for common activity patterns
parts:
Hi all,

I've opened a thread on GitHub [1] to identify common activity
patterns and propose the implementation of helpers for them. Quick
example: it is quite common to set an attribute as a counter or
identifier that needs to be incremented/decremented over time. So
instead of

trajectory() %>%
set_attribute("parts", function() get_attribute(env, "parts") + 1)

it would be nice having something like

trajectory() %>%
add_to_attribute("parts", 1)

There are other examples in [1]. I invite everyone to discuss here and
propose there (please, do not discuss on GitHub to keep the issue
clean) other patterns you may use. Any idea would be greatly
appreciated.

[1] https://github.com/r-simmer/simmer/issues/124

Regards,
Iñaki

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: Helpers for common activity patterns
parts:
I've created a new package called 'simmer.bricks'. It is aimed to
provide wrappers for common activity patterns. This initial version
implements visit(), wait_until() and delayed_release(). To test it,
you need to install it from GitHub (using remotes or devtools) along
with the development version of simmer:

remotes::install_github(c("simmer", "simmer.bricks"))

Any feedback would be very welcome.

Iñaki

> Hi,
>
> How would you set as an attribute the cumulative increase in the counter?

Do you mean a vector of successive updates? It is not possible, but
the attributes can be monitored (if mon=2 in the corresponding
generator), so if you call get_mon_attributes and filter by attribute,
you get exactly that.
